The musical segment with Mavis Staples was loud and incomprehensible. She and some other musicians -- Susan Tedeschi, Ben Folds, and a bunch of other famous names Colbert yelled out at the end who I couldn't quite get -- performed "Everyday People" with Colbert's house band. But what is this affirmative-action thing where every white late night host has to have a black jazz-fusion bandleader now? Fallon's got Questlove Thompson and the Roots, Kimmel I don't know (but I'm guessing so); even Leno had Kevin Eubanks (Branford Marsalis first, Ricky Minor towards the end), but at least they performed songs that everyone knew leading up to commercial. This guy plays a fucking keytar or something, or one of those weird hybrid keyboard-clarinet things that the '80s band "The Hooters" was named for (no, it wasn't boobies). No Paul Shaffer is this guy, Jon Baptiste. Probably some zydeco musician Colbert was friends with back home in the Palmetto State. 2/5 from my perspective. I'd rather watch old man Dave nap in his front-porch rocking chair at the farmhouse in Montana. Or Jay polish his Studebaker. Or Craig Kilborn try to get out of witness protection. But, for anyone who hasn't seen it, YMMV. Just my 2c.
